Utility-First: Tailwind's utility-first approach uses small, composable classes for styling directly in HTML. Instead of writing custom CSS, you combine utilities like flex, text-center, and p-4 to build designs.

Setup: Tailwind is installed via npm and configured through tailwind.config.js. The PostCSS plugin processes the CSS directives, scanning your source files for class usage to generate the final stylesheet.

npm install -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer
npx tailwindcss init -p
Configuration: The tailwind.config.js file controls content paths, theme extensions, variants, and plugins. Custom values can extend the default theme without overriding the complete design system.

Flexbox: Tailwind provides comprehensive flexbox utilities including flex-direction, justify-content, align-items, and flex-wrap. Responsive variants allow different flex behaviors at each breakpoint.

Grid: Tailwind's grid utilities enable CSS Grid layouts with grid-cols, grid-rows, and gap classes. Items can span multiple columns or rows using col-span and row-span utilities.

Spacing: Spacing in Tailwind uses a consistent scale for margin, padding, and gap classes. The scale ranges from 0 to 96, with values like p-4 (1rem), mx-auto (auto margins), and gap-8 (2rem).

Sizing: Width and height utilities follow the spacing scale plus fractional and viewport values. Classes like w-full, h-screen, max-w-7xl, and min-h-screen handle common sizing needs.

Font: Tailwind provides font-family, font-size, font-weight, and font-style utilities. Classes like font-sans, text-lg, font-bold, and italic compose to create typographic styles.

Text: Text utilities cover alignment, decoration, transform, and overflow. Truncation, line-clamping, and text wrapping classes handle common text layout challenges.

Alignment: Tailwind's text alignment and vertical alignment classes work alongside flex and grid for precise text positioning. Text can be aligned left, center, right, or justified.
Lists: List style utilities control markers, position, and indentation. Tailwind provides list-none, list-disc, list-decimal, and list-inside/list-outside for ordered and unordered lists.

Custom Colors: Custom colors are added through the theme.extend.colors configuration. Tailwind generates shades from 50 to 900 automatically, or you can define exact hex values for each shade.
Color Palette: Tailwind's default palette includes eight color families (gray, red, yellow, green, blue, indigo, purple, pink) each with 11 shades. Colors are applied via bg-*, text-*, border-*, and ring-* utilities.
Colored element
Dark Mode: Dark mode is enabled via the darkMode config option. The dark: prefix applies styles only when dark mode is active, either via class strategy or media query.

Breakpoints: Tailwind uses five default breakpoints: sm (640px), md (768px), lg (1024px), xl (1280px), and 2xl (1536px). Breakpoint prefixes conditionally apply styles at specific viewport widths.
Responsive text size
Mobile-First: Tailwind follows a mobile-first approach where unprefixed utilities apply to all screen sizes. Larger screen overrides use breakpoint prefixes like md: or lg: to modify the base styles.
Responsive Patterns: Common responsive patterns include stacking on mobile and side-by-side on desktop, hiding/showing elements per breakpoint, and adjusting spacing or typography across viewports.

Buttons: Tailwind buttons combine padding, colors, borders, and hover states. Focus rings ensure accessibility, and disabled states convey inactive buttons with reduced opacity.

<button class='px-6 py-2 bg-blue-600 text-white rounded-lg hover:bg-blue-700 focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 disabled:opacity-50'>
  Click me
</button>
Cards: Cards are built with rounded corners, shadows, padding, and dividers. Tailwind's utility classes compose to create consistent card components with header, body, and footer sections.

Modals: Modals use fixed positioning, backdrop overlays, and z-index utilities. Transitions and transforms create smooth open/close animations using Tailwind's transition utilities.

Forms: Form elements are styled with consistent padding, borders, and focus states. Tailwind provides form-specific classes for inputs, selects, textareas, checkboxes, and radio buttons.

<input class='w-full px-4 py-2 border border-gray-300 rounded-md focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500' />
<select class='block w-full mt-1 rounded-md border-gray-300 shadow-sm'>
  <option>Option 1</option>
</select>

Custom Plugins: Tailwind plugins allow adding new utilities, components, or base styles programmatically. Plugins use the addUtilities, addComponents, addBase, and matchUtilities API functions.
Directives: Tailwind's CSS directives (@tailwind, @apply, @layer, @config) control how styles are generated and applied. @apply inlines utility classes into custom CSS, while @layer organizes styles.
Functions: Tailwind provides theme(), screen(), and other CSS functions. theme() accesses design tokens from the config, while screen() generates media query strings for custom CSS.

PurgeCSS: Tailwind automatically removes unused CSS in production by scanning content files. The content array in config specifies the paths to scan, resulting in dramatically smaller CSS bundles.
JIT Mode: Just-in-Time mode (now default in v3) generates styles on-demand as you author HTML. This eliminates unused CSS entirely, enables arbitrary values like top-[117px], and speeds up builds.
Arbitrary values in JIT mode
Bundle Size: Tailwind's production builds typically result in CSS files under 10KB after purging. The built-in minification and tree-shaking ensure only the utilities you actually use end up in the final bundle.

# Check bundle size
npx tailwindcss -i ./src/input.css -o ./dist/output.css --minify
# Typical result: 3-10KB
